1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))

Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'

1 under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees,
tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are recorded cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no. 41/4(2 12), 45/18 (504), 13 (416) total land measuring 11 bigha and 12 biswas (in short, the said land)
having share as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.

5. It is stated that the petitioners are only persons entitled to receive the compensation amount as per the actual prevailing market rate of the said LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Prem Singh
& ords. v. Union of India
Page no. 3 of 12 land.
The actual physical possession of the said land has not been taken till the filing of the petitioner.
It is stated that the said award is not acceptable and the Award amount has been received under protest and without prejudice to their rights.

There is one Keekar tree aged about ten years in the said land and the same have became useless due to the acquisition of the said land in as much as the petitioners have also spent more than Rs. 10,000 on it.

The trees weigh more than 20 quintal and the rate of wood is @
Rs. 500 per quintal.

6. It is stated that the petitioners has levelled the said land throughout having means of irrigation and were reaping three healthy crops in a year including the seasonal vegetables in between and the cattle feeds and were earning about Rs. 1 lakh per acre per year from selling the agricultural produce after retaining them for their domestic use.

The said land is surrounded by the well developed the areas having all basic modern facilities i.e. well connected roads, adequate transport facility,
hospitals, schools, colleges, reputed clubs, farmhouses, party lawns and banquet Halls and is,
therefore, having the market value @ Rs. 8000 per square yards and the agricultural land was sold at this rate in the surrounding areas.

The NH 10 is 2 kms away from the said land, the bottling plant of Indian Gas and FCI godown is around 3 kms from the said land, and Mundka, Udyog Vihar,
metro workstation is around 2 kms from the said land, Railway Station Mundka and other developed areas having all the transport facilities and basic amenities
are around 1 kms from the said land.
LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 7.

sentences.text: 8. It is stated that the agricultural land bearing Khasra no. 815, measuring 4 bigha 1 biswa situated in the village Hiran Kudna was sold for the consideration amount of Rs. 48 lakhs by Sh. Mool Chand in favour of Sh. Ganga Bishan Gupta vide sale deed dated 20.09.2000, which is hardly 2 km away from the said land and having same level and potential and the similar status as the said land.

The agricultural land in Khasra no. 815 measuring 4 Bigha 16 Biswa situated in the village Hiran Koodna was sold for the consideration amount of Rs. 75 lakhs by Sh. Ganga Bishan Gupta in favour of Smt.
Sumitra Devi vide sale deed dated 05.08.2003, which is 2 kilometers away from the said land.

The agricultural land bearing Khasra no. 378 (416), 390(003), 391(413), 392(416) total admeasuring 14 Bigha 08 Biswa situated in village Savda was sold for the consideration amount of Rs. 1,87,50,000 by Sh. S.N. Gupta in favour of Smt. Sumitra Gupta vide sale deed dated 08.092003 which is hardly 2.5 km from the said land and having same potential and similar status as of the said land.

9. It is stated that the ld. LAC while determining the market value of the said land has failed to rely upon the said sale deeds and discarded the same on the false grounds that the said land is at a very far distance from LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh

& ords. v.
Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 village Hiran Kudna and Savda and their potentially also differs.
It is also submitted that ld. LAC failed to appreciate that it is the distance and the potentiality of the land and not the village, which is to be kept in mind while awarding the compensation.

It is stated that the ld. LAC failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10%
yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.

10. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000 per square yards and that too only to hose who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which shows that that the land for residential and commercial purposes was not so easily available @ Rs. 6000 per square yards.

The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped the land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/turn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioners.
11. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money and the ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioners.
The ld. LAC has grossly erred in deducting the tax, as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.

It is stated that the petitioner is claiming the compensation for the said land @ Rs. 8000 per square yards and also entitled to compensation amount of Rs.
30,000 on account of the abovementioned three, boring as well as one well.

The LAC no. 163 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 petitioner also claims lumpsum amount of Rs. 1 lakh per acre along with interest for loss and damages.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party,
therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.
It is stated that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
15. It is submitted that the possession of the land has not been handed over to the DDA on 06.09.2005 and after taking possession same was transferred to RPDVII.
It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld.

LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation,
therefore, the petitioners are not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & ords. v. sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
18. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED TO ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO TO WHAT AMOUNT?
OPP LAC

163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 19.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
20.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Ram Kishan (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
21. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

22. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

entities.text: Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

23. In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ram Kishan (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).

This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Sh. Prem Singh vs Union Of India on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11548693/
5 Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 24. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

25. It is pertinent to mention here that Smt. Nirmala, LRs of Sh. Jagbir Singh has given her separate statement to the effect that she is relinquishing her share in favour of her brother Sh. Joginder.
LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 RELIEF 26.

entities.text: Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
27.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.

25. It is pertinent to mention here that Smt. Nirmala, LRs of Sh. Jagbir Singh has given her separate statement to the effect that she is relinquishing her share in favour of her brother Sh. Joginder.
LAC no. 163 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & ords. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 RELIEF 26.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
